evidence.positive: Ingested a Mayo SIU^S14 case file plus In Room / Anes Start / Out Room timing events through the running app's admin HL7 send endpoint (tenant mayo-mayo) for case 305901 in room 'RM OR BEDSIDE ROMB 01'; the app persisted it in "mayo-mayo".operations with start_time 2026-10-26 18:10 and end_time 19:55 (closed case). Ran the shipped orci/src/main/analytics/mayo-mayo/create_analytics_views.sql (HEAD 10f82fe08) verbatim against the app's own Postgres with psql -f. mayo_operation_rooms_v returned the row 'RM OR BEDSIDE ROMB 01 | ROMB | SAINT_MARYS | cardiac=f | excluded=t', and case 305901 was absent from both mayo_operations and mayo_shared_metric_operations_v. lifetime_counts.sql (dates filled 2026-10-01..2026-11-01) returned num patients 2 / num operations 2, i.e. the bedside case was not counted.
evidence.negative: Same ingest path for three control cases: 305902 in 'RM OR 107 ROMB 01 528' (normal Saint Marys OR), 305904 in 'RM OR BEDSIDE ROEI 01' (a bedside room NOT named in excluded_rooms), and 305903 in 'RM OR 508 ROMB 01 600' (cardiac, already excluded pre-fix). Under the shipped views, mayo_operation_rooms_v flagged 107 and ROEI bedside as excluded=f and cardiac=f, and both 305902 and 305904 appeared in mayo_operations and mayo_shared_metric_operations_v and were the two operations lifetime_counts counted; 305903 stayed excluded via cardiac=t as before. So the exclusion is exact-name only: it removes the ROMB 01 bedside record and nothing else, and does not disturb the cardiac exclusion.
evidence.red_check: Data+code flip. Re-ran the parent commit's version of create_analytics_views.sql (957cf1314^, which has no excluded_rooms list) against the same app database, then while those pre-fix views were live ingested a second bedside case through the app (case 305909, control id OR3059REDCHECK-BEDSIDE, room 'RM OR BEDSIDE ROMB 01', with timing events). Under the pre-fix views mayo_operation_rooms_v had no excluded column, and both bedside cases 305901 and 305909 appeared in mayo_operations and mayo_shared_metric_operations_v; lifetime_counts rose to num patients 4 / num operations 4 (RED). Reverted by re-running the shipped file: the excluded column returned with 'RM OR BEDSIDE ROMB 01' = t, both bedside cases vanished from mayo_operations and the metric cohort, and lifetime_counts fell back to 2 / 2 while the base table "mayo-mayo".operations still held both bedside rows (the exclusion is in the view, not the data). The app log line 'Received HL7 message: type=SIU^S14, controlId=OR3059REDCHECK-BEDSIDE' exists only from the red-check ingest.

caveats: Views were executed on the instance's Postgres 14.5; the two CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... NULLS NOT DISTINCT statements at the end of the file (PG15+ syntax, unchanged by this ticket) failed there, so the rollup unique indexes and the refresh-role grants were not exercised. Every view and materialized view above them was created and queried.
Metabase itself was not reached; the SQL was run with psql against the app database, and lifetime_counts.sql was run with its {{START_DATE}}/{{END_DATE}} variables substituted by hand.

Only the Mayo views and lifetime_counts were queried directly. The 13 other Mayo report files were checked by grep to read mayo_operations or the metric cohort rather than "mayo-mayo".operations, so they inherit the exclusion, but each was not run individually.

Epic OAuth is not configured in this instance, so the post-timing-event patient refresh logged EpicOAuthException for every SIU; the operations and their start/end times were already persisted, so this did not affect the validation.

automation.assessment: No automated coverage exists for orci/src/main/analytics; the views are only exercised in Metabase. The exact-name exclusion is cheap to lock in with a throwaway-schema SQL test: load one operation per room shape, run the shipped file, and assert mayo_operations membership. The valuable assertions are the negative ones (ROEI bedside and the ordinary ROMB rooms must stay) and the base-table reconciliation (the excluded case is still in "mayo-mayo".operations).
proposed_tests: Testcontainers (postgres:17) test that creates the mayo-mayo base tables, inserts operations for 'RM OR BEDSIDE ROMB 01', 'RM OR BEDSIDE ROEI 01', 'RM OR 107 ROMB 01 528' and 'RM OR 508 ROMB 01 600', runs create_analytics_views.sql via psql/JDBC, and asserts mayo_operation_rooms_v.excluded is true only for the ROMB 01 bedside row
Same fixture: assert mayo_operations and mayo_shared_metric_operations_v contain the 107 and ROEI-bedside cases and neither the ROMB-01-bedside nor the cardiac 508 case
Same fixture: assert lifetime_counts.sql (variables substituted) counts exactly the two included operations and that "mayo-mayo".operations still returns all four rows
Same fixture, can-it-fail guard: temporarily CREATE OR REPLACE mayo_operations without the excluded predicate and assert the bedside case reappears, then re-run the shipped file

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: A case filed under RM OR BEDSIDE ROMB 01 was ingested through the app and, after running the shipped Mayo views SQL, was flagged excluded and absent from mayo_operations, the metric cohort, and the lifetime counts.
Negative: Cases in a normal Saint Marys OR and in the ROEI bedside room stayed in every view and were counted, and the cardiac room remained excluded as before.
Red check: Re-running the pre-fix views SQL while ingesting a second bedside case made both bedside cases appear in mayo_operations and raised the lifetime count from 2 to 4, and re-running the shipped SQL removed them again.

Automation: No coverage exists for the analytics SQL; a Testcontainers fixture asserting room flags and cohort membership for the four room shapes is proposed.
